newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil prepares for Norwegian Sea spud.
newsitem.headline: Statoil prepares for Norwegian Sea spud.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil said on Thursday its first exploration well on the Vema Dome in the Norwegian Sea is due to be spudded in September from the rig Ocean Alliance.
Awarded in last year's 15th offshore licensing round, this acreage in the Voering Basin lies in 1,100-1,400 metres (3,609-4,593 ft) of water.
"Because of local weather conditions we aim to spud by September 15," geologist Arnt Roernes told Status Weekly newsletter. "Drilling should take about three months."
The Vema Dome is about 20-25 km (12-16 miles) west of the Nyk Ridge, where British Petroleum spudded an exploration well this week, the newsletter said.
Also being drilled by Ocean Alliance, this operation's outcome will probably influence the siting of Statoil's well, it said.
Norsk Hydro ASA will use the same rig during the summer to drill further south on its Ormen Lange prospect in the Norwegian Sea's Moere Basin.
Statoil will then take over Ocean Alliance before it passes to Norske Shell for drilling on Helland Hansen west of the Heidrun field off mid-Norway around the New Year.
